en-US.description: Open-source desktop workbench for digital forensic analysis
en-US.name: Crush
en-US.releaseNotes:
> Focus: Chromium Disk Cache, FlatBuffers and Core Data stores; protected and split UFDR reports; bundled peach updated to v0.11.0.
Highlights
- Chromium Disk Cache — Simple and Blockfile caches (HTTP, WebView, Cronet, CacheStorage, Code Cache) open in their own viewer, with headers, times, certificates and bodies.
- FlatBuffers — supported in parsers, viewers and the BLOB Inspector, either schema-less (heuristic) or with a .fbs/.bfbs schema.
- Core Data — the SQLite viewer shows Core Data stores, including entities, relationships, model and persistent history.
- Cellebrite UFDR — protected (encrypted) reports open directly or prompt for their password; split ZIP/UFDR sets (.z01, .z02, …) open from any part.
- C2PA — the Media Viewer shows Content Credentials for audio and video files.

Notable fixes
- Evidence integrity — an SQLite database inside an archive, backup or disk image no longer picks up a -wal/-journal file from the examiner's own computer.
- macOS app — no longer reported as damaged (@CyberMike81, #182).

Behaviour changes
- C2PA row — names where a scan stopped and lists unevaluated C2PA data under C2PA scan notes.

Bundled tools
- peach v0.11.0 — the interface can now be translated, with German as the first translation, and the AUL rule pack grows from 51 to 53 rules. Re-tag existing AUL sessions to apply them. See the peach v0.11.0 release notes.
Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md
